qualityBar.verdict: A grim strategy game where keeping one battered unit alive can matter more than recruiting a whole new army.

set.longDescription:
Disciples II Gold puts you in charge of a small army in a world that looks as if every kingdom has been cursed separately. The Empire, Mountain Clans, Legions of the Damned and Undead Hordes each have campaigns and distinct rosters. A hero leads the group across a map, claims territory, gathers treasure and chooses battles that will shape what the surviving units become. The atmosphere is rich in dark fantasy detail, but the important decisions are wonderfully practical: which fight is worth the injuries, and which upgrade path will leave a squad ready for the next one?

Unlike a strategy game where soldiers are disposable numbers, individual Disciples units gain experience and change into stronger forms. The buildings in your capital determine possible upgrades, so a choice made away from the battlefield can decide whether a wounded survivor becomes the specialist you need. That gives even a modest encounter a little tension. A hero can be carried between scenarios, making campaigns feel like a long trip rather than unrelated maps. Gold bundles the base game and expansion material, including Rise of the Elves, into one purchase.

The official GOG page lists the Gold edition as a 2005 Windows release and marks both single-player and multiplayer. The original Disciples II manual documents hotseat for two to four players and TCP/IP play over LAN or the internet. Those modes matter, but they do not automatically establish a working PlayBound virtual-LAN route. We have not verified this particular GOG build end to end with the PlayBound party network, so its page explains the native modes without promising one-click joining or a dedicated server. The old Draft FAQ called it single-player only; that was wrong. A mouse and keyboard remain the documented control route, with no verified native controller mode or PlayBound Controls profile.

GOG provides a DRM-free offline installer, so Galaxy is optional. Its current stated minimum is Windows 10, a 1.8 GHz CPU, 2 GB of RAM and a DirectX 9.0c-compatible 3D card. GOG does not provide a recommended tier or a precise disk figure in the same listing, so the hardware section leaves those fields unfilled. We also avoid treating a temporary store discount as part of the game's name, as the old auto-generated FAQ did.

The appeal is the way its battles remember your choices. You may win a fight, then spend the next turn mourning the unit that was one experience point from its next form. Disciples II Gold has plenty of old PC strategy roughness, but its faction art, linked campaigns and unit progression give patient players a reason to see one more scenario through.
set.whyWePickedIt: Few fantasy strategy games make a single unit upgrade feel so consequential. Gold brings the campaigns and expansions together in a DRM-free package, and the native hotseat and network modes give friends several ways to compete once we verify a PlayBound party path.
set.thatOneThing: A soldier survives a battle with one hit point, earns a promotion, and suddenly the entire war plan depends on keeping him alive.

installSteps.text: Buy Disciples II Gold on GOG and download the Windows offline installer from your library. GOG Galaxy is optional.
Run the GOG installer, then use PlayBound Locate to select the installed game folder. PlayBound does not redistribute the commercial files.
Launch the game and choose a campaign, skirmish or multiplayer option. Check display and input settings on your PC before a long session.

firstPlaySteps.text: Start a faction campaign, inspect the unit upgrade tree at your capital, and keep experienced survivors with the hero who trained them.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: For same-PC multiplayer, choose Hotseat from the game's Multiplayer menu and take turns. The original manual documents two to four players.

For separate PCs, use the game's TCP/IP connection option. This GOG build has not yet been verified with PlayBound's virtual-LAN party handoff; coordinate the address and connection in the game itself.
